## Issue #6 UI Follow-Up Requirements

Issue [#6](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/6) adds these UI requirements to the demo surface:

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R26 | Start the browser demo in interactive demo mode by default. | Implemented by initializing demo mode to `true`. |
| R27 | Update the next-dialog timer every second. | Implemented with `demoCountdown` state updated by a one-second interval. |
| R28 | Hide diagnostics unless diagnostics mode is enabled. | Implemented with a default-off diagnostics toggle gating trace, intent, evidence, worker status, and thinking steps. |
| R29 | Keep the default chat transcript focused on user-visible messages. | Implemented by hiding diagnostic chips and evidence in normal mode. |
| R30 | Preserve issue data and analysis under `docs/case-studies/issue-6`. | Implemented with raw GitHub data, the issue screenshot, online research, requirement extraction, and solution notes. |

## Issue #8 Telegram Bot Requirements

Issue [#8](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/8) adds a Telegram chat surface and asks the assistant to report execution evidence for code answers.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R31 | Provide a simple Telegram bot interface. | Implemented as `POST /telegram/webhook` on the existing Rust HTTP server. |
| R32 | Route Telegram prompts through the same symbolic engine used by other interfaces. | Implemented by calling `FormalAiEngine` from the Telegram webhook handler. |
| R33 | Support private Telegram chats. | Implemented and tested with a private `chat.id`. |
| R34 | Support public Telegram chats. | Implemented and tested with a supergroup-style negative `chat.id`. |
| R35 | Preserve code formatting in Telegram replies. | Implemented by converting markdown code fences to escaped Telegram HTML `<pre><code>` blocks. |
| R36 | Compile or run generated code blocks where the environment supports it. | Implemented through `rust/src/execution_box/`: Telegram selects only an explicitly configured host sandbox or the paired `start-command` Docker runner; browser execution is limited to a runtime the user loaded. |
| R37 | Report output and execution status to users. | Implemented with `execution_evidence::Evidence` carrying exact argv, exit status and observed-output hash; the localized answer cites its evidence id. |
| R38 | Report environment limitations instead of silently claiming execution. | Implemented from observed probes: absent configuration refuses in all five supported languages, and `NotProbed` is distinct from unavailable. |
| R39 | Keep timeout behavior bounded and visible. | Implemented by `ExecutionBox`: elapsed time, deadline and partial output are retained; the descending-N policy records every attempted rung and has a ten-minute hard failure. |
| R40 | Keep the web interface aware of execution limitations. | Implemented by the browser runtime probe: it shows runtime/download size, requires an explicit load action, and labels output observed only after execution. |
| R41 | Preserve issue research and raw evidence under `docs/case-studies/issue-8`. | Implemented with raw GitHub data, online research, local tool records, solution options, and verification notes. |
| R42 | Run the Telegram bot from the CLI using long polling by default. | Implemented as `formal-ai telegram` defaulting to `--mode=polling` and calling Telegram's `getUpdates` with offset, timeout, limit, and `allowed_updates` controls. |
| R43 | Keep the webhook server available as an opt-in CLI mode. | Implemented as `formal-ai telegram --mode=webhook`, which delegates to the existing `serve` HTTP route on the same host/port flags. |
| R44 | Publish the Telegram CLI in a Cargo crate. | Implemented by keeping the `formal-ai` binary and library in the published `formal-ai` crate; `cargo install formal-ai` exposes the `telegram` subcommand. |
| R45 | Use `lino-arguments` with clap-style configuration for all CLIs. | Implemented through `lino_arguments::Parser` derive and `lino_arguments::init()` in `main`, so flags read from CLI, environment variables, and `.lenv`/`.env` files consistently. |
| R46 | Make the Telegram polling loop testable without a network. | Implemented through the `TelegramTransport` trait and a `ScriptedTransport` test double covering offset advancement and invalid-payload recovery. |
| R47 | Log polling lifecycle events for operators. | Implemented through `eprintln!` lines that announce loop start, transport failures, invalid payloads, successful sends, send failures, and loop stop. |

## Issue #14 Unified-Surface Requirements

Issue [#14](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/14) requires every
interface to use the same universal solver, expands the solver's specialized
handlers to cover arithmetic, concept lookup, JavaScript execution, and
conversation memory, and persists the demo's UI state in Links Notation.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R83 | Route every demo answer through the same universal solver as the library, CLI, HTTP server, and Telegram bot — no hardcoded prompt→answer table in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker.js`. | Implemented by rewriting `js/worker/formal_ai_worker.js` so the worker runs greeting, identity, arithmetic, concept-lookup, recall, JavaScript-execution, hello-world, and unknown-fallback handlers that mirror `rust/src/solver.rs`. |
| R84 | Persist demo on/off and diagnostics toggles in `localStorage` using Links Notation so the UI state remains portable and human-readable. | Implemented by `js/preferences.js` (load/save/format/parse around the `formal-ai.preferences.v1` key with `demo_preferences` root) and wired into `js/app.js`. |
| R85 | Solve arithmetic prompts (symbols, English-word operators, parentheses, decimals, modulo) without hardcoding answers; report division-by-zero rather than panic. | Implemented by `calculation_expression_candidates`/`evaluate_calculation` in `rust/src/calculation.rs`, the local fallback in `rust/src/arithmetic.rs`, and `try_arithmetic` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/mod.rs`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/reasoning_paths.rs::arithmetic_*` and mirrored in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker.js`. |
| R86 | Answer "what is X?" / "tell me about X" / "define X" from a seeded Wikipedia/Wikidata/Wiktionary concept table and always cite the source. | Implemented by `data/seed/concepts.lino`, `CONCEPTS`/`lookup_concept`/`extract_concept_term` in `rust/src/solver_helpers/`, and `try_concept_lookup` in `rust/src/solver.rs`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/reasoning_paths.rs::concept_lookup_*` and mirrored in the demo worker. |
| R87 | Remember the conversation: recall the user's name, the previous question, and summarize prior turns through the solver, with prior turns recorded as `prior_turn:` events. | Implemented through `ConversationTurn`, `ConversationRole`, and `UniversalSolver::solve_with_history` in `rust/src/solver.rs`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/reasoning_paths.rs::solve_with_history_*`; the demo passes `history` to the worker. |
| R88 | Declare JavaScript execution capability explicitly: the Rust solver explains it has no JS runtime, the browser demo actually runs the snippet in a Worker sandbox and reports stdout/return value/errors. | Implemented by `extract_javascript_program`/`extract_fenced_block` in `rust/src/solver_helpers/`, `try_javascript_execution` in `rust/src/solver.rs`, and the worker's `tryJavaScriptExecution` handler; covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/reasoning_paths.rs::javascript_*`. |
| R89 | Compile case-study evidence (issue body, comments, PR comments, online research, requirement-to-solution mapping) under `docs/case-studies/issue-14/`. | Implemented in `docs/case-studies/issue-14/README.md` with raw data in `docs/case-studies/issue-14/raw-data/`. |

## Issue #18 Full-Memory Export/Import Requirements

Issue [#18](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/18) reports that
the **Export memory** button on the deployed demo saves only the in-session
event log, not the full agent state. The requirements below make full-memory
exports the universal default on every surface and surface known data
migrations on import.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R109 | The default **Export memory** action must always produce the full, self-contained agent state (seed + memory log + UI preferences + environment metadata + version). No second button click is required to get the full export. | Implemented by `FormalAiMemory.exportFullMemory({ seed, events, preferences, info })` in `js/memory.js` (wired to the topbar `Export memory` button via `handleExportMemory` in `js/app.js`) and by the Rust mirror `memory::export_full_memory` in `rust/src/memory.rs` (used by `formal-ai memory export` as the new default). |
| R110 | Imports must accept both the legacy `demo_memory` document and the new `formal_ai_bundle` document so old exports continue to work. | Implemented by `FormalAiMemory.importFullMemory` (browser) and `memory::import_full_memory` (Rust). Both auto-detect the document header and fall back to the legacy `demo_memory` parser when no bundle header is present; covered by `import_full_memory_accepts_legacy_demo_memory` in `rust/src/memory.rs`. |
| R111 | After import, surface known data migrations (e.g. seed-version mismatch) directly in the UI so the user can take action without reading code. | Implemented by `FormalAiMemory.suggestMigrations` (browser) and `memory::suggest_migrations` (Rust). `handleImportMemory` in `js/app.js` appends the resulting suggestions to the memory-status indicator; the CLI `memory import` / `bundle import` commands print each suggestion via `eprintln!("Migration: <message>")`. |
| R112 | The prefilled "Report issue" body must instruct users to wrap the `.lino` export in a `.zip` (GitHub does not yet accept `.lino` attachments), and must explicitly remind users to redact sensitive content before attaching. | Implemented by the **Attach full memory (optional)** section of the shared report builder: the sentence itself is `issue_report_memory_note` in `data/seed/agent-info.lino`, it names `formal-ai-memory.lino`, references the `.zip` workaround and the redaction reminder inline, and links to [`docs/upload-memory.md`](../../upload-memory.md) for the full walkthrough (issue #78 collapsed the previous three-paragraph block into one line + docs link so the encoded URL fits under GitHub's 8192-byte cap). Issue #839 moved the emission out of the browser into `rust/src/issue_report.rs` (mirrored for the browser by `js/app/issue-report.js`), so the CLI and desktop reports carry the same line. |
| R113 | The CLI surface (`formal-ai memory export`, `formal-ai bundle export`) and the Rust library API must default to full-memory output as well, so every interface stays consistent. | Implemented by switching `formal-ai memory export` to write the full `formal_ai_bundle` by default in `rust/src/main.rs`; `--events-only` opts back into the legacy `demo_memory` shape. `formal_ai::export_memory_full`, `import_memory_full`, `suggest_memory_migrations`, `BundleInfo`, and `ParsedBundle` are re-exported from the crate root in `rust/src/lib.rs`. |
| R114 | Keep VISION.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, README.md, and the e2e/unit tests in lockstep with the new defaults so the documentation, the requirement matrix, and the regression coverage all describe the same behavior. | Implemented by this row plus the **Single-File Reproducibility** paragraph in `VISION.md`, the export/import notes in `README.md`, the rewritten `Export memory downloads a Links Notation file` Playwright e2e in `rust/tests/e2e/tests/multilingual-memory-settings.spec.js` (now asserting `formal_ai_bundle` + `seed_files`), and the new `memory::tests::full_memory_round_trip_*` / `suggest_migrations_*` unit tests. |

## Issue #78 Shorter Issue Reporting Requirements

Issue [#78](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/78) reports
that the prefilled `Report issue` URL overflows GitHub's 8192-byte
`/issues/new?body=…` limit (mobile shows *"Whoops, something went wrong!"*,
desktop shows *"Whoa there! Your request URL is too long."*). The
requirements below shrink the prefilled body until it fits, by moving the
long memory-upload instructions into a single docs page and by recording
the dialog as a compact `U:` / `A:` code block.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R115 | The prefilled `Report issue` body must keep the encoded `body=` query parameter under GitHub's request-line limit so the new-issue page actually opens for typical sessions (no more *"URL is too long"*). | Implemented by collapsing the three-paragraph **Attach full memory** block into one sentence + docs link, and by rendering the dialog as a single fenced code block instead of a per-message subsection loop. `createIssueReportBody` in `js/app/main.jsx` gathers the facts and `renderReportBody` (`js/app/issue-report.js`) emits them; `fitIssueUrl` still drops earlier turns until the encoded URL fits. The compact form is exercised by `experiments/issue-78-dialog-format.mjs` and asserted by the e2e tests below. |
| R116 | The dialog transcript embedded in the prefilled body must use a single fenced code block with `U:` / `A:` line prefixes, instead of one Markdown subsection per message, while still preserving the focused-message marker and the assistant `intent` annotation when the assistant could not classify the prompt. | Implemented by the **Reproduction of dialog** section of the shared builder (`rust/src/issue_report.rs`, mirrored by `js/app/issue-report.js`), which also picks a fence long enough to contain the dialog. The block opens with `issue_report_dialog_legend` from `data/seed/agent-info.lino` — `Legend: \`U\` = user, \`A\` = agent, \`T\` = tool result.` since #839 gave the agentic surface tool results to report; known-intent turns stay as plain `A: …` to match the issue example, and the focused-message marker plus the `intent` annotation only appear inline for the `unknown` intent (`A (intent: unknown, reported): …`) where they actually carry diagnostic value. Covered by the `known assistant dialogs include a prefilled issue report link` and `unknown prompts include a prefilled missing-rule issue link` tests in `rust/tests/e2e/tests/demo.spec.js`. |
| R117 | The verbose upload-memory instructions (Gist / `.zip` / per-OS walkthroughs / redaction reminders) must live in a single page checked into the repository so the prefilled body only needs a one-line pointer with a link. | Implemented by [`docs/upload-memory.md`](../../upload-memory.md) and the matching link in the **Attach full memory (optional)** section the shared builder emits. The topbar `Report issue` and `Export memory` tooltips also point at the same doc instead of repeating the workflow. |
| R118 | Documentation must explain that users can either upload the full memory export to a GitHub Gist (no extension restrictions) or wrap it in a `.zip` (GitHub's issue uploader still rejects raw `.lino`). | Implemented by the *Step 3 — Attach the file (choose one)* section of `docs/upload-memory.md`, which documents both Option A (Gist) and Option B (`.zip`) and links the GitHub attachment-types doc as the upstream constraint. |
| R119 | The e2e regression suite must enforce all of the above: the prefilled body must contain `docs/upload-memory.md`, the dialog must use the seeded `Legend: …` block, and the old verbose per-OS Compress / Send-to instructions must be absent. | Implemented by extending `Report issue link is present in the topbar and links to the upload-memory guide (R112 + issue #78)` in `rust/tests/e2e/tests/multilingual-chat.spec.js` (asserts `docs/upload-memory.md` and forbids the per-OS Compress / Send-to phrases) and by tightening the prefilled-body assertions in `rust/tests/e2e/tests/demo.spec.js`. |

## Issue #117 Lino I18n Catalog Requirements

Issue [#117](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/117) asks the
browser UI to stop using its own i18n implementation and instead use
[`link-foundation/lino-i18n`](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n),
with nested Links Notation authoring, multiline quoted strings, full language
parity, CI enforcement, and case-study evidence.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R137 | Browser UI translations must be loaded through `link-foundation/lino-i18n`, not through a hand-maintained JavaScript translation/interpolation implementation. | Implemented by `js/i18n.js`, which takes `lino-i18n@0.3.0` from its tree-shakeable `lino-i18n/browser` entry (bundled by `js/vendor-entry.js`), loads `js/i18n-catalog.lino` together with `js/i18n-catalog-permissions.lino` and `js/i18n-catalog-messages.lino` (split so each file stays under the Links Notation line limit) through `loadCatalogs`, which fetches them concurrently and merges their per-locale keys in order, and creates the runtime with `createI18n`. The import map in `js/index.html` is pinned to the same package version. |
| R138 | UI translation source must use nested Links Notation and multiline quoted strings for long entries. | Implemented in `js/i18n-catalog.lino`, where `buttons`, `titles`, `composer`, `settings`, `status`, and trace messages are nested under top-level locale blocks and long tooltip values use `"""` strings. |
| R139 | English, Russian, Chinese, and Hindi must all contain the same complete UI key surface. | Implemented by migrating all 104 existing UI keys into each locale block in `js/i18n-catalog.lino`, including parent-label keys such as `settings.language` via the upstream `label` convention. |
| R140 | CI/CD must fail when the i18n catalog loses a required key, adds a non-label drift key, drops a locale, or contains empty translations. | Implemented by `rust/tests/e2e/scripts/check-i18n-catalog.mjs` and the `Check i18n catalog coverage` step in `.github/workflows/release.yml`, run as `npm run --prefix rust/tests/e2e check:i18n`. |
| R141 | Runtime tests must prove the browser uses the published `lino-i18n` package and can resolve nested catalog entries, parent labels, interpolation, and fallback. | Implemented by updating the Issue #94 Playwright tests in `rust/tests/e2e/tests/demo.spec.js` to expect `lino-i18n@0.3.0` and adding a nested catalog lookup test for Issue #117. |
| R142 | Compile issue #117 evidence, online research, requirements, solution plan, and verification notes under `docs/case-studies/issue-117/`. | Implemented in `docs/case-studies/issue-117/README.md` with raw captured GitHub, npm, release, and upstream README data under `docs/case-studies/issue-117/raw-data/`. |

## Issue #159 Hive Mind Lookup and Curated Project Summarization

Issue [#159](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/159) reported
that "What is Hive Mind?" / "Что такое Hive Mind?" prompts fell through to
the Wikipedia closest-match fallback and surfaced unrelated pages such as
LOIC. The PR comments expanded the scope: deduplicate and simplify project
descriptions through a formalize → summarize → deformalize pipeline that
drops installation noise, keep purpose / language / stars / why-useful
statements, expose configurable lengths (`Topic` 1–5 words, `Short` ~20%,
`Standard` ~50%, `Full` 100%, `Expand` ~200%), and use Natural Semantic
Metalanguage primes plus compound-word substitution when the configuration
requests them. The same pipeline must back project descriptions, dialog
summaries, chat titles, and URL content.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R195 | "What is Hive Mind?" must prefer `link-assistant/hive-mind` before any web-search closest-match fallback in every supported language when associative project promotion is enabled. | Implemented by the generic `try_project_lookup` path in `rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests.rs`, which matches the `hive mind` / `hivemind` aliases against the project registry and renders a language-aware promoted answer. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/project_lookups.rs::russian_hive_mind_prompt_prefers_link_assistant_project` and the matching English test. |
| R196 | Hive Mind / project answers must be generated from a reviewable seed file rather than hard-coded strings, so adding or editing a project is a data change. | Implemented by `data/seed/projects.lino` (15 curated Link Assistant / Link Foundation / LinksPlatform projects with weighted statements, localisations, repository URLs, topic labels, and aliases) and the `ProjectsRegistry` reader in `rust/src/seed/projects.rs`; the browser worker loads the same records through `js/seed_loader.js`. |
| R197 | A configurable summarization pipeline must expose `formalize`, `summarize`, and `deformalize` stages so the same code can drive topic labels, short descriptions, standard answers, full text, and expanded explanations. | Implemented by `rust/src/summarization/mod.rs` with `Statement`, `StatementKind`, `SummarizationMode` (`Topic` / `Short` / `Standard` / `Full` / `Expand`), `SummarizationConfig`, and the `formalize` / `summarize` / `deformalize` / `to_topic` / `describe_project` functions. Covered by unit tests in `rust/src/summarization/mod.rs::tests`. |
| R198 | Compressed answers must filter out boilerplate (install / example) sentences and keep the highest-weighted purpose, language, and feature statements. | Implemented by `StatementKind::is_boilerplate` plus `SummarizationConfig::drop_boilerplate` (default `true`) and the weight-descending sort in `summarize`. |
| R199 | Configurable compound-word substitution and Natural Semantic Metalanguage primes must be available so callers can shorten chat titles or expand explanations from the same configuration. | Implemented by `apply_compound_words` (compound-word shortening) and `apply_semantic_primes` (NSM substitution table for English and Russian); `Expand` mode appends NSM paraphrases to the surviving statements. |
| R200 | The project handler must run after `concept_lookup` so existing seed-backed concepts (Links Notation, Wikipedia, …) keep their answers, while promoted repository aliases such as Hive Mind are treated like any other project record. | Implemented by invoking `try_project_lookup` immediately after the `concept_lookup` method point in `rust/src/meta_method_dispatch.rs::try_dispatch`; there is no dedicated Hive Mind handler. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/project_lookups.rs::curated_project_concept_prompt_routes_to_project_lookup` (uses `link-cli`). |
| R201 | Every promoted project answer must log the summarization configuration so the trace explains both what was matched and how the text was compressed. | Implemented by `render_project_lookup` emitting `project:promoted`, `summarization:mode`, `summarization:language`, `source` (the project URL), and the consulted web-search providers. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/project_lookups.rs::curated_project_lookup_records_summarization_evidence`. |
| R202 | The summarization pipeline must accept raw README markdown, strip badges / HTML comments / fenced code blocks / heading markers before classification, and feed the remaining prose through the same `formalize` / `summarize` / `deformalize` stages. | Implemented by `strip_markdown_noise`, `formalize_markdown`, and `describe_readme` in `rust/src/summarization/mod.rs`. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs::strip_markdown_noise_drops_badges_html_comments_and_code_blocks`, `formalize_markdown_classifies_install_and_purpose_lines`, `describe_readme_short_keeps_purpose_drops_install`, and `describe_readme_topic_returns_repo_slug`. |
| R203 | Multi-turn dialogs must be summarizable through the same pipeline, biasing user turns above assistant turns so a short summary keeps the user's questions. | Implemented by `DialogTurn`, `formalize_dialog`, and `summarize_dialog` in `rust/src/summarization/mod.rs` (user turns weigh +20, assistant turns weigh -10). Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs::formalize_dialog_biases_user_turns_above_assistant_turns` and `summarize_dialog_short_keeps_user_questions`. The conversation-summary intent now runs through this pipeline (`rust/src/solver_handlers/conversation_memory/conversation_summary.rs::try_summarize_conversation`) and logs `summarization:mode`, `summarization:language`, and `chat_title` events; existing reasoning-paths tests still pass. |
| R204 | Generating a 1-5 word chat title must reuse the same pipeline in `Topic` mode so titles never drift from the body summary. | Implemented by `generate_chat_title` (wraps `summarize_dialog` with `SummarizationMode::Topic`). Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs::generate_chat_title_returns_five_or_fewer_words`. |
| R205 | When `try_http_fetch` receives a URL pointing to a curated GitHub repository, the response must surface the curated description through the summarization pipeline and emit explicit trace evidence. | Implemented by `match_curated_github_url` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests.rs`: the handler invokes `describe_project` in `Standard` mode and logs `http_fetch:curated_project`, `summarization:mode`, and `summarization:language` evidence. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/project_lookups.rs::http_fetch_of_curated_github_url_describes_project_via_summarization` and `http_fetch_of_unknown_url_skips_curated_project_summary`. |
| R206 | The default cap on retained statements after summarization must be a documented constant (30) that any caller can override via `SummarizationConfig::with_max_statements`. | Implemented by `DEFAULT_MAX_STATEMENTS = 30` in `rust/src/summarization/mod.rs` and `SummarizationConfig::effective_max_statements`. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs::default_max_statements_is_thirty` and the existing `effective_max_statements_*` unit tests. |
| R207 | The 5 summarization modes must match the documented size targets (topic = 1-5 words, short ≈ 20%, standard ≈ 50%, full = 100%, expand ≈ 200%). | Implemented by `SummarizationMode::target_percent`. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs::summarization_mode_target_percent_matches_vision`. |

## Issue #438 Prepared Telegram Docker Image

Issue [#438](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/438) asks for a
fully prepared Docker image for the Telegram bot so the system can be started
with minimum configuration, ideally from a single shell line. PR
[#470](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/470) turns the existing
Docker-in-Docker runtime into a release-published image and records the
operator path in docs and tests. The follow-up maintainer comment additionally
asks for one-click start/stop of both the Telegram bot container and the
OpenAI-compatible agentic server container from the desktop app, with the same
flow documented for server operators.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R320 | Issue #438 research, issue metadata, PR metadata, comments, CI context, related PRs, online research, and reproduce-before-fix logs must be preserved under `docs/case-studies/issue-438`. | Implemented by `docs/case-studies/issue-438/README.md` and `docs/case-studies/issue-438/raw-data/*`, including `repro-before-docker-runtime.txt`, `repro-before-release-workflow.txt`, and `repro-before-docs-traceability.txt`. |
| R321 | Releases must publish a prepared Telegram Docker image to an always-available default registry without requiring Docker Hub secrets. | Implemented in `.github/workflows/release.yml` by publishing `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:latest` and the version tag to GitHub Container Registry with `packages: write` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` after the crate is visible. The runtime image also declares `org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai` in `Dockerfile` for repository-linked package metadata. |
| R322 | Operators must be able to start the polling Telegram bot from a single shell line with only `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` as required configuration. | Implemented by documenting `docker run --rm --privileged -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc -v formal-ai-telegram-docker:/var/lib/docker ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:latest` and by preserving `CMD ["formal-ai", "telegram", "--mode", "polling"]` in `Dockerfile`. |
| R323 | The repository must provide a compose file that starts the prepared image, enforces the token requirement, and persists the inner Docker daemon state. | Implemented by root `compose.yaml`, which defaults to `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:latest`, requires `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, and mounts `formal-ai-telegram-docker:/var/lib/docker`. |
| R324 | Existing local-build and optional mirror paths must stay available for development and operators who cannot use GHCR. | Implemented by retaining the local `docker build -t formal-ai .` instructions, preserving the Sysbox runtime example, keeping optional Docker Hub publishing in `.github/workflows/release.yml`, and supporting `FORMAL_AI_DOCKER_IMAGE` in `compose.yaml`. |
| R325 | Release notes must advertise the prepared container artifact alongside crates.io/docs artifacts. | Implemented by `scripts/create-github-release.rs`, which accepts `--ghcr-url`, renders a GHCR badge, and still supports `--docker-hub-url` for optional mirrors. |
| R326 | Tests must keep the prepared image startup, release publication, and issue documentation contracts synchronized. | Implemented by `rust/tests/unit/docker_runtime.rs::compose_file_runs_prebuilt_telegram_image_with_minimum_configuration`, `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/release_publishing.rs::release_workflow_publishes_prebuilt_ghcr_image_after_crate_is_visible_and_optional_docker_hub_mirror`, and `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements.rs::issue_438_prebuilt_telegram_image_documents_are_present_and_traceable`. |
| R327 | The desktop app must start and stop both prepared services — the Telegram bot and the OpenAI-compatible API server — with one click, polling Docker for live status and requiring `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` before the bot starts. | Implemented by `desktop/lib/service-control.cjs` (dependency-injected `runDocker`, `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}'` status, stale-container reaping, required-token check), exposed over IPC by `desktop/main.cjs` (`formalAiDesktop:serviceStatus`/`startService`/`stopService`), bridged by `desktop/preload.cjs`, and rendered as the sidebar Services panel in `js/app.js`. |
| R328 | A server must reproduce the identical containers with one line, and the two Docker-in-Docker services must not collide. | Implemented by root `compose.yaml`, which adds an opt-in `server` profile (`docker compose --profile all up -d`) running `formal-ai serve` on `127.0.0.1:${FORMAL_AI_SERVER_PORT:-8080}`, and gives each service its own inner-Docker volume (`formal-ai-telegram-docker`, `formal-ai-server-docker`) because two DinD daemons cannot share one `/var/lib/docker`. |
| R329 | The one-click desktop and one-line server paths must be fully documented and kept synchronized by tests. | Implemented by `docs/desktop/service-control.md` (plus README "One-click services" and ARCHITECTURE "One-click / one-line services"), and verified by `desktop/scripts/service-control.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/unit/specification/desktop_surface.rs::{desktop_service_control_starts_and_stops_prepared_containers,desktop_web_surface_exposes_one_click_service_controls}`, and `rust/tests/unit/docker_runtime.rs::compose_file_offers_optional_openai_compatible_server_profile`. |

## Issue #703 External-Agent Orchestration

Issue [#703](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/703) and the
maintainer follow-up on PR
[#876](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/876#issuecomment-5127332907)
require Formal AI to become the explicit controller of external agents:
registered and requested custom clients, bounded workspaces, parallel
comparison and composition, replayable evidence, exact-session correction,
meta-language synthesis, requested-language output, fact cross-checking, and
learning from completed work. The implementation keeps execution,
fact-verification, translation, and learning grants visible rather than
conflating model confidence with authority.

JavaScript twin (PR #1188, 2026-10-08, JavaScript-first doctrine R997): the whole controller is ported to `js/agentic/crate/orchestration_*.mjs` (permission, workspace, runner, attribution, dispatch, incremental, session file, analysis, beside the existing replay verifier), with `recursive_execution.mjs`, `task_decomposition_tree.mjs`, `client_contract_learning.mjs`, `seed_client_integrations.mjs`, the synthesis pipeline (`summarization_dedup.mjs`, `summarization_importance.mjs`, `summarization_recheck.mjs`, `relative_meta_logic.mjs`, `statement_verification.mjs`, `translation_formalization.mjs`) and the CLI twin `js/agentic/orchestration_cli.mjs` (`run`, `dispatch`, `resume`, `synthesize`, `learn`, `replay`, the flags of `rust/src/cli_orchestration.rs`). `rust/tests/web/issue-0703-orchestration-{run,dispatch,committed,analysis}.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-0703-synthesis-pipeline.test.mjs` replay the Rust integration tests over a node stand-in agent and real `git`, and recompute the committed #703/#924/#933 sessions, ledgers and learning documents byte for byte. Not yet at parity: the legs that go through `formal-ai with` and its loopback health server (no JavaScript twin; the runner launches `$FORMAL_AI_CONTROLLER_PROGRAM` or `formal-ai` where Rust uses `current_exe`), the `merge_into_context`/`gather` world-model layer, `balanced_split` and `Decomposition::from_links_notation`; the synthesis claims and verdicts the JavaScript council test pins were derived from the algorithm, not from a native run, because no prebuilt binary carries the `synthesize` command.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R703-1 | External agents must be denied by default and receive only an explicit canonical workspace, hard timeout, captured output/effects, and reviewable provenance. | `AgentRunPermission`, `workspace`, `runner`, and canonical hash-chained `AgentSession` records implement the boundary; timeout kills the Unix process group and records one failed attempt. Covered by permission, containment, timeout, no-retry, effect, and replay tests in `rust/tests/integration/issue_703_orchestration.rs`. JavaScript twin pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-0703-orchestration-run.test.mjs` (`R703-1: a timeout is recorded once, kills the process, and is never retried`). |
| R703-2 | Drive Agent CLI, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, and OpenCode from a data-defined adapter registry, against loopback Formal AI or existing vendor authentication. | Implemented: `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` carries editing, structured-output, and resume argv; `AgentTarget::{FormalAi,Vendor}` selects the target. The deterministic six-entrypoint test drives the public CLI; the real-client matrix is opt-in because it needs each vendor's own authentication. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_703_orchestration.rs` (`all_six_cli_entrypoints_run_a_scripted_repo_task_through_the_real_wrapper`, `seed_registry_pins_each_clients_exact_native_resume_contract`, `all_required_seed_adapters_capture_process_and_workspace_events`, `direct_vendor_entrypoints_keep_editing_and_prompt_arguments`). JavaScript twin pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-0703-orchestration-run.test.mjs` (`R703-2: all six registered adapters capture process and workspace events`). |
| R703-3 | Decompose a task into bounded leaves, dispatch them, verify their work, and compose only passing non-conflicting effects. | Implemented: `orchestration::dispatch` uses the universal task decomposer, isolated copies, argv-based executable-allowlisted verification, drift revalidation, conflict detection, and transactional composition. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_703_orchestration_followup.rs` (`universal_decomposition_dispatches_independent_leaves_in_parallel`, `decomposition_never_composes_changes_from_a_failed_agent`, `verification_commands_must_be_explicitly_allowlisted`, `comparison_refuses_to_overwrite_workspace_drift_after_candidates_fork`) and `rust/tests/integration/issue_703_controller_boundaries.rs` (`leaves_writing_different_bytes_to_one_path_are_refused_by_name`). Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_703_orchestration_followup.rs` (`parallel_comparison_records_a_ledger_and_composes_the_winner`, `winner_selection_is_deterministic_for_a_recorded_ledger`, `committed_parallel_comparison_ledger_records_the_selected_winner`, `dispatch_joins_every_worker_before_returning_an_error`) and `rust/tests/integration/issue_703_orchestration.rs` (`comparison_cli_succeeds_when_one_verified_winner_passes`). Unknown executables, an argv without `{task}`, and registered-label grant bypasses are rejected; public single/multi Bash regressions prove the surface. A changed reported id fails. All six resume argv contracts and the real Agent CLI `--resume ID --no-fork` chain are byte-pinned. | R703-7 | Capture complete sessions and replay them byte-for-byte, detecting edits, truncation, reordering, or broken ancestry. | Implemented, JavaScript first: canonical pretty JSON, terminal newline, event sequence, previous-event links and event SHA-256 are checked on replay, and the session fields the events stand for are bound to them (one terminal outcome matching `status`, `workspace_effect` events equal to `changes`, a continuation exactly when a native session was resumed), so an edited event, an edited status or effect list, a dropped tail event, reordering and byte truncation are each rejected by name. `replay_continuation` replays a correction only against the exact parent bytes its digest names, so broken ancestry, including a parent whose free-text stdout was edited, is rejected. Free-text fields are bound by that parent digest and the committed bytes, not by the event chain. ## Issue #839 Full-Conversation Issue Reports

Issue [#839](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/839) reports
that an agentic `report issue` filed nothing a maintainer could act on: issue
[#838](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/838) carried 271 KB of
base64 HTTP proxy traffic instead of the conversation, named a session no
harness had ever heard of, was cut mid-record by `tail -c 12000`, attached a
gist literally named `formal-ai-report.XXXXXX.lino`, and reported success
throughout. The requirements below make the agentic report the same document
the web reporter has always produced, and make every way of failing loud.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R494 | A report must export the caller's real harness session, not a value derived from the conversation's text. | The HTTP server records `x-formal-ai-dialog-id` per request (`rust/src/dialog_log.rs`), `report_issue.rs::dialog_id` reads it, and falls back to `--session latest` — which `formal-ai context session` resolves from the live harness — rather than to a hash. Covered by `conversations_sharing_a_first_message_do_not_collide`, `the_session_subcommand_resolves_the_session_this_shell_is_inside`, and `two_conversations_sharing_a_first_message_file_different_contexts`. |
| R495 | A named `--source` that cannot be exported must fail loudly instead of degrading to a different capture. | `rust/src/cli_context.rs` errors on an unexportable named source and on an export with no `message` records; the generated script runs under `set -eu`, so nothing reaches `gh`. Covered by `harness_source_fails_loudly_instead_of_returning_the_server_log`, `an_empty_export_fails_instead_of_reporting_success`, and `an_unexportable_session_fails_before_gh_is_reached`. |
| R496 | The server must record a conversation, distinct from the HTTP proxy trace, so `--source server` and `--source both` mean something. | `rust/src/dialog_conversation.rs` writes one conversation record per exchange alongside the proxy frames; `both` merges the harness and server records into one document. Covered by `server_export_carries_conversation_turns_not_only_proxy_frames` and `both_merges_harness_and_server_records_into_one_document`. |
| R497 | One shared builder must produce the identical report document for web, CLI, desktop, Telegram, and VS Code. | Delivered: `rust/src/issue_report.rs` owns the six sections and the title; `js/app/issue-report.js` mirrors it for the wasm worker, which cannot link the Rust core, and `js/app/main.jsx` only gathers facts and labels. `rust/tests/integration/issue_839_report_parity.rs` renders the same fixture through both and fails on drift. |
| R498 | The title must quote what the conversation was about: drop the report request itself, quote `` `first` + `last` `` when two subjects fit, otherwise the first alone on a word boundary, and never the bare default while a user turn exists. | `issue_title` in `rust/src/issue_report.rs`; covered by `two_subjects_are_titled_first_plus_last`, `a_single_subject_is_quoted_on_its_own`, `an_oversize_subject_is_truncated_on_a_word_boundary`, `an_answered_report_request_can_still_be_a_subject`, and `the_default_title_is_never_used_when_a_user_turn_exists`. |
| R499 | Truncation must never cut inside a Links Notation record; oversize context attaches in full with an explicit `omitted N` marker. | `truncate_records` in `rust/src/issue_report.rs` keeps whole records from both ends and names the count it dropped; `--oversize gist` uploads the complete context, `--gist-visibility` is an explicit documented choice (`docs/report-issue.md`). Covered by `truncation_never_splits_a_links_notation_record` and `a_byte_slice_of_the_same_export_loses_the_record_boundaries`. |
| R500 | The generated script must be a real, testable program: every command verified with `command -v`, every scratch path a real filename. | `rust/src/agentic_coding/report_script.rs` renders `set -eu`, a `command -v` preflight per program, and a `mktemp -d` scratch directory removed on exit. Covered by `a_missing_command_fails_loudly_and_files_nothing`, `the_scratch_template_is_expanded_before_anything_is_written`, and the end-to-end `the_generated_script_files_the_full_conversation_in_all_six_sections`, which executes the script against a stubbed `gh` and asserts on the file `gh issue create` actually received. |

## Issue #909 Headless-Ready Global Client Configuration

Issue [#909](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/909) reports that
`formal-ai with <tool> --global` wrote shell exports and nothing else, so gemini
(`Invalid auth method selected`) and qwen (`No auth type is selected`) still
refused to start headlessly while `--global` reported success and exited 0. The
per-run path already wrote both missing pieces; only the global path had drifted.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R909-1 | `--global` must materialise every file the client needs for a headless start, not only shell exports, driven by the client registry. | Implemented by the `companion "<path>"` global-config node in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` (gemini's `~/.gemini/settings.json` with `security.auth.selectedType`), parsed by `parse_companion_file` and written, backed up, and undone by `write_companion_file` alongside the primary file (landed for R916-08a); guarded here by `global_gemini_writes_the_settings_file_that_selects_an_auth_type` and `global_gemini_preserves_and_restores_an_existing_settings_file`. |
| R909-2 | The OpenAI-compatible clients must receive the complete auth triple, including `OPENAI_MODEL`. | Implemented by `shell_env "OPENAI_MODEL={model}"` in qwen's `global` block (landed for R916-08b); guarded here by `global_qwen_writes_the_complete_openai_triple`. |
| R909-3 | `--global` must not report success when the configuration it just wrote cannot start the client. | Implemented by `rust/src/client_integrations/global_verify.rs`: `verify_written_config` re-reads every seed-declared `headless_require` from the files on disk and fails with `client_global_config_requirement_missing`; the opt-in `--verify` runs `probe_headless_start`, which starts the client once non-interactively and fails on a seeded `auth_refusal`. Guarded by `verify_fails_when_the_configured_client_refuses_to_start`, `verify_succeeds_when_the_configured_client_starts`, `verify_is_rejected_without_global`, and the unit tests in `global_verify.rs`. |
| R909-4 | The headless contract must be declared as data, apart from the settings that write it, so verification reads back the result instead of trusting the writer. | Implemented by the `headless_require "<kind>=<target>"` and `auth_refusal "<text>"` seed entries and their `ClientIntegrationGlobalConfig::headless_requirements` / `ClientIntegrationCompanionFile::headless_requirements` / `ClientVerification::auth_refusals` fields; `issue_909_headless_global_configuration_is_traceable` guards the registry shape. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/headless_client_configuration.rs`. |
| R909-5 | The gap and its closure must be reproducible without a live client. | Implemented by `experiments/issue-909-headless-config-gaps.sh`, which runs `--global` into a throwaway `HOME` and reports every missing headless requirement per tool. |
| R909-6 | The composition of R909-1..R909-4 must break the build, not only each requirement in isolation. | Implemented: Guarded by the whole-task test `global_all_leaves_every_client_headless_ready_and_probed`: one `--global --all --verify` sweep must satisfy every requirement the registry declares, read back from the files on disk, and the same sweep must fail when a probed client answers with an auth refusal. |
| R909-7 | A generated seed block's shard must be a function of that block alone, so a change to one block cannot dirty the rest of `data/seed`. | Raised in review on this issue: `scripts/close-total.py` filled `closure-generated-NN.lino` sequentially up to a line cap, so each shard depended on the total size of everything sorted before it and one new token dirtied 11 of 11 shards. Implemented by `shard_for(slug)`, which places a meaning by `sha256(slug) % SHARD_COUNT`; guarded by `generated_closure_shards_are_content_addressed` and measured across four sort positions by `experiments/issue-909-seed-shard-conflict-blast-radius.sh`. |

# Issue #1154: One Shell-Argument Reading for the Whole Agentic Module

Issue [#1154](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1154) (E119):
Codex's shell tool `exec_command` sends the command under the argument key
`cmd`, while `progress.rs` read only `command`. The work-item read was never
recorded as attempted, and the stateless planner re-derived the identical
`gh issue view` call 78 times in a row (6.2M input tokens) until the client
compacted the thread. The full incident account, with the transcript excerpts,
is `docs/case-studies/issue-1154/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1154-1 | One shared `command_argument` for the whole `agentic_coding` module, reading the argument key from the client's declared tool schema (the key whose schema describes the shell command), falling back to `command`, `cmd`, `script`, and an array form joined for `shell`-style tools; the seven local copies are deleted. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/tool_result.rs` holds the one shared `command_argument` (string and joined-array forms, `command` → `cmd` → `script`), and the seven former copies in `progress.rs`, `file_read.rs`, `tool_result.rs`, `narration.rs`, `command_reroute.rs`, `evidence_record.rs` and `workspace_change.rs` delegate to it (JS twin `commandArgument` in `js/agentic/tool_result.mjs`). The schema reading is wired since 2026-10-07: `command_argument_key` resolves the property whose own schema describes the shell command (never the working-directory property), and `project_declared_command_keys` (JS `projectDeclaredCommandKeys`) projects the request's tool definitions onto the transcript before planning, so a call whose tool declares its command under another key (e.g. `shell_command`) carries that value under `command`; the projection is pure (no state between requests, client messages untouched) and runs at both servers' agentic entry (`agentic_outcome` in `rust/src/protocol.rs`, `agenticOutcome` in `js/server/agentic.mjs`). Pinned by `the_command_key_is_read_from_the_tool_schema` and `a_schema_declared_key_plans_exactly_as_the_command_key` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs` (drafted without a local cargo run) and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1154-command-argument.test.mjs` (8 tests passing locally, including the server entry). |
| R1154-2 | Invariant independent of parsing: never plan a tool call whose name and arguments are byte-identical to one already attempted in the current turn window; if the planner would, report the stuck step and its last result instead of repeating it. | Implemented: `Progress::repeated_call` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/progress.rs`, JS `Progress.repeatedCall` in `js/agentic/progress.mjs`) recognizes a completed call by byte-identical arguments or the same canonical command/URL operand (the protocol layer may project `command` onto `cmd` before the transcript echoes the call), and `stop_repeated_call` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/planner.rs`, JS `stopRepeatedCall`) replaces the repeat with the `stuck_step_report` answer from `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino`. A completed call is the loop signature; a failed one keeps its existing bounded retry and the two-failure stop of issue #1133. Pinned by `repeated_successful_read_is_reported_not_replanned` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs` and by the R1154-2 cases of `rust/tests/web/issue-1154-command-argument.test.mjs`. |
| R1154-3 | After a successful read, the fetched text drives `plan_work_item_execution` exactly as on the Claude and Agent paths. | Implemented by the shared reading: `issue_view_url` resolves under `cmd` (and under a schema-declared key through R1154-1's projection), the read lands in `fetched_pages`, and `repository_work_item_objective` feeds `plan_work_item_execution` unchanged. Pinned by `codex_cmd_read_drives_execution_instead_of_repeating` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs` and its JS twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1154-command-argument.test.mjs`. |
| R1154-4 | Tests: replay the Codex transcript's first two Responses items (`function_call` `exec_command {"cmd": …}` + `function_call_output`) through the Responses input conversion and assert the next plan is not another `gh issue view`; a table test over `{command}`, `{cmd}`, `{script}`, `{command:[…]}` yields the same recorded read. | Implemented in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs`: the replay goes through `ResponsesRequest::to_chat_completion_request` (the server's own conversion), and the table covers all four spellings plus the twice-repeated transcript shape. |

## Issue #1161 Client Registry Names the Agent Config Env

Issue [#1161](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1161) (E126)
makes the client registry declare *how* a client is pointed at its config —
the env var that relocates it — instead of implying an `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
relocation that also moves `gh`'s and git's config and breaks GitHub
authentication inside the session. The incident analysis, the per-client
evidence, and the fix live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1161/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1161-1 | Every `global_configs` entry in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` can declare the environment variables that relocate its own config file (`config_env "VAR"` children), parsed into a new `ClientIntegrationGlobalConfig::config_env: Vec<String>`; entries whose file has no relocation variable declare an empty list. | Implemented: the `config_env` field and parser arm in `rust/src/seed/client_integrations.rs`, filled in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` (and its committed `rust/embedded/` mirror) only where in-repo evidence exists. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1161_client_registry_environment.rs`. |
| R1161-2 | `agent` names `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG` (config file) and `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR` (directory); `codex` and the `t3code` OpenAI-protocol entry name `CODEX_HOME`; `opencode`, `opencode-vscode` and `opencode-desktop` name `OPENCODE_CONFIG` and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`. | Implemented in the same seed file. Evidence per client: agent — the issue itself and the wrapper's own `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_CONTENT` one-shot mechanism; codex — `docs/configuration/output-sessions.md` (`$CODEX_HOME/sessions/…`), `experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/README.md` (`CODEX_HOME` → a directory holding `config.toml`) and `rust/tests/t3code_launch.rs`; t3code — its own ephemeral block relocates the same `config.toml` via `CODEX_HOME` (`docs/configuration/t3-code.md`); opencode family — each block's own ephemeral `config_env "OPENCODE_CONFIG"` / `config_dir_env "OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR"`. Pinned by the per-client assertions in the same test file. |
| R1161-3 | The declaration is a registry surface: `formal-ai clients --format json` carries it additively as `global_configs[].config_env` (plus the one-shot `config_env`/`config_dir_env`/`config_content_env`/`temp_home_env` top-level fields), and `formal-ai clients` prints it on each `global[...]` line. | Implemented in `rust/src/cli_clients.rs` and tested against the built binary: `rust/tests/integration/issue_1161_clients_surface.rs` runs `formal-ai clients --format json` and asserts, for every seeded client, that each `global_configs[].config_env` and the one-shot `config_env`/`config_dir_env`/`config_content_env`/`temp_home_env` fields equal the parsed seed and that `verification.surface` is still present (`clients_json_carries_each_global_config_relocation_variable`), and runs `formal-ai clients` and asserts each client's `global[...]` line ends with ` via <variables>` exactly when it declares some (`clients_text_prints_the_relocation_variables_on_each_global_line`). Additive only — the matrix (`experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/run_leg.sh`) still reads exactly the `verification.*` fields it read before. |
| R1161-4 | A host integration contract is documented: a host that needs a task-local client config sets the declared variable and must not relocate `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` (the 2026-09-27 `gh`-auth incident, link-assistant/hive-mind#2314). | Implemented: the "Host integration contract" section and the *Relocate via* column in `docs/configuration/agentic-clis.md`, the registry-surface note in `docs/testing/agentic-cli-tools.md`. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1161-host-contract.test.mjs`, which reads the declared variables from `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` and asserts that the contract's bullet for each declaring client names every one of its variables, that the clients declaring none are named as such, that the *Relocate via* column lists every declared variable, and that the section forbids relocating `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` and cites link-assistant/hive-mind#2314. |
| R1161-5 | Clients whose global entry is a shell profile (`gemini`, `claude`, `qwen`, `aider`) or a fixed path with no evidenced variable (`cursor`, `grok`) declare none; no variable is fabricated. | Implemented and pinned by `entries_without_a_relocation_variable_declare_none` in the same test file. |
| R1161-6 | Hive Mind switches its Formal AI agent launcher from the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` relocation to `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR`/`LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG`. | Implemented in Hive Mind and confirmed from this repository on 2026-10-07: link-assistant/hive-mind commit de14357623 ("fix(#2314): keep gh authenticated in the Formal AI tool env", 2026-09-27) makes `buildFormalAiClientEnv` in `src/formal-ai-runtime.lib.mjs` set `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR` (agent) and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` (opencode) to the directory of the registry's `global_configs[].path` instead of relocating `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, with the regression test `tests/formal-ai-tool-env-keeps-gh-auth-2314.test.mjs`; hive-mind#2314 closed as completed on 2026-09-28, and the commit is an ancestor of the hive-mind release v2.33.14. This repository's side of the contract — a JSON global config that declares that `*_DIR` variable for each client the launcher maps, and no client declaring `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` — is pinned by `R1161-6: every JSON-configured client Hive Mind launches keeps its *_DIR variable` in `rust/tests/web/issue-1161-host-contract.test.mjs`. |
| R1161-7 | The declared relocation actually works end to end: the agent CLI is started with `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG(_DIR)` pointing at a temporary config directory and serves the session from it (pull-request follow-up row: the smoke test half of the registry surface). | Implemented and run in CI: `case_relocated` in `experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/run_leg.sh` runs for every headless CLI client whose global config declares `config_env`. It writes the config with `formal-ai with --globally` into a scratch home, copies the written directory to a temporary one, and starts the real CLI directly. The run uses an empty `HOME` and only one declared variable, which points at the copied directory (`*_DIR`/`*_HOME`) or file (the others). The case asserts that the session reaches `formal-ai serve` through the recording proxy and that nothing is written back into `HOME`. For `agent` this runs `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG` and `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR`. Pinned by `the_matrix_leg_serves_a_session_from_each_declared_relocation_variable`. Its first matrix run (37594789426) passed for `codex` (`CODEX_HOME`). For `agent` it showed that the relocated config is loaded and its `formalai` provider found, but the CLI's own default model outranks the config's `model`. The case therefore passes the model the way `formal-ai with` does, reading the new `model_arg`, `model_selector` and `model_arg_after_first_arg` fields of `formal-ai clients --format json`. With that, agentic CLI matrix run 37638262565 (head bb8759cdb, job "E2E (agent)" 112855726572) passed both agent relocations: `ok relocated: agent served a session from LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG=…/opencode.json` and `… from LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR=…`. Pinned by `the_matrix_leg_serves_a_session_from_each_declared_relocation_variable` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1161_client_registry_environment.rs`. |

## Issue #1181 Standalone CLI Binaries and Consistent Boolean Env Switches

Issue [#1181](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1181) (E146,
part of the #1183 umbrella) has two halves: people cannot *run* the released
CLI at all (the release ships desktop apps and a VSIX but no standalone
`formal-ai` binary — the only channels are a full `cargo install` source build
or a 24.3 GB container image, #1153), and the one env switch that gates CLI
output rejects the conventional `1`/`0` spellings (`FORMAL_AI_SILENT=1
formal-ai chat …` fails with `invalid value '1' for '--silent' [possible
values: true, false]`). The evidence, the design, and the per-file change list
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1181/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1181-1 | `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` gains a `cli` job that builds `formal-ai` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and uploads one archive per target to the same GitHub Release the `build`/`vscode` jobs publish to. | Implemented and tested as a mechanism: the `cli` job in `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` (five-leg matrix mirroring the `build` job's needs/concurrency/if/permissions/checkout/sccache conventions, `taiki-e/setup-cross-toolchain-action@v1` for the musl legs because the dependency graph compiles C code) uploads each archive with `gh release upload` to the tag `resolve` picked. `scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh` now requires the archives of every `label: cli-*` matrix leg (read from the workflow, not a second list) before its idempotency guard skips a release, so a release that has the desktop set but lacks a CLI archive is rebuilt instead of staying partial. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1181-cli-release-assets.test.mjs` (the matrix is exactly the five requested targets; the resolver script, run with a recording `gh`, rebuilds a release without the CLI archives and skips a complete one) and by `workflow_run_builds_when_release_is_missing_cli_archives` in `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/desktop_release_resolve.rs`. What only the next tagged release can show: its asset list carries the five `formal-ai-cli-*` archives, which needs the real cross-builds on the five runners. |
| R1181-2 | Each archive is named `formal-ai-cli-<target-triple>.tar.gz` (`.zip` for the Windows target), contains the `formal-ai` binary plus `LICENSE` and `README.md` under a top-level `formal-ai-cli-<triple>/` directory, and is reproducible from `cargo build --release --target <triple> --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai --locked`. | Implemented and tested as a mechanism: the "Build formal-ai CLI binary" step runs the exact pinned-lock command; `rust/tests/web/issue-1181-cli-release-assets.test.mjs` executes the job's own "Package the CLI archive", "Smoke test CLI archive" and "Collect CLI checksum fragment" step scripts with a stand-in binary and asserts the archive holds `formal-ai`, `LICENSE` and `README.md` under `formal-ai-cli-<triple>/`, that the smoke test runs the extracted binary's `--version`, and that the fragment is one `sha256sum`-format line naming the archive. What only a release run can show: the real binaries for all five targets (the `.zip` leg runs PowerShell's archiver on the Windows runner). |
| R1181-3 | The `finalize` job's consolidated `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt` cover the five CLI archives alongside the existing desktop/VSIX assets, in the same files, with the same "INCOMPLETE" honesty reporting for partial matrices. | Implemented and tested as a mechanism: `cli` joins `finalize`'s `needs`; each leg uploads a `SHA256SUMS-cli-<label>.partial` fragment (the `cli-` label prefix prevents collision with the desktop legs' identically-shaped labels in the merged `fragments/` directory); the `builder_of` map and label loop in `finalize` carry every `cli-*` label mapped to its runner. `rust/tests/web/issue-1181-cli-release-assets.test.mjs` checks the map and loop against the matrix and executes the finalize manifest step on a CLI fragment with a recording `gh`: the archive's line lands in `SHA256SUMS.txt`, `BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt` names its builder, and the legs that produced nothing are reported as `INCOMPLETE` with `incomplete=` in the step output. The consolidated files on a real release appear with the next tagged release. |
| R1181-4 | `rust/Cargo.toml` gains a `[package.metadata.binstall]` table so `cargo binstall formal-ai` resolves one of the R2 archives without a source build. | Implemented and tested: `[package.metadata.binstall]` (`pkg-url` …/`formal-ai-cli-{ target }.tar.gz`, `pkg-fmt "tgz"`, `bin-dir "formal-ai-cli-{ target }/{ bin }{ binary-ext }"`) with a `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` override to the `.zip`; the URL is written out literally because the archive name ends `.tar.gz`, not binstall's default `{ archive-suffix }` (`.tgz`). `rust/tests/web/issue-1181-cli-release-assets.test.mjs` fills the templates for every matrix leg and asserts the URL is `releases/download/v<version>/<the archive the workflow uploads>`, the format matches the archive and `bin-dir` is the binary's path inside it. A real `cargo binstall formal-ai` resolves once the next tagged release carries the archives. |
| R1181-5 | `scripts/install.sh`'s `install_cli()` and `install.ps1`'s equivalent download and verify the matching `formal-ai-cli-<target>` archive first, falling back to `cargo install formal-ai` only when no matching archive exists for the host's OS/arch (e.g. windows-arm64, which R1 does not build). | Implemented and tested: `install_cli_prebuilt`/`Install-CliPrebuilt` resolve the host triple, fetch the archive, verify it against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt` through the existing `verify_checksum`/`Test-Checksum` helpers, run the installed binary's `--version`, and only then report success; any unavailable/failed prebuilt path falls back to the unchanged `cargo install` body. `rust/tests/web/issue-1181-cli-release-assets.test.mjs` runs `scripts/install.sh cli` against a stand-in GitHub (recording `curl`, fixed `uname`, recording `cargo`) with the archive the workflow's package step built: it installs and runs the binary without calling `cargo`; a checksum mismatch aborts with nothing installed and no `cargo` fallback; a host no leg builds (Linux riscv64) falls back to `cargo install formal-ai` without downloading an archive. It also checks that both installers map hosts only to matrix targets, and parses `install.ps1` with PowerShell's parser where `pwsh` is installed (the Linux runner of `layered-ci.yml`; this macOS workstation has none, so the parse runs in CI only). |
| R1181-6 | A single boolean-env parser accepts `1/0/true/false/yes/no/on/off` case-insensitively (surrounding whitespace tolerated; anything else is unrecognised, never silently coerced), is the `value_parser` for every clap arg with `env = "FORMAL_AI_*"` on a `bool` field, and is used by every ad-hoc `std::env::var("FORMAL_AI_*")` boolean read in `rust/src`. | Delivered and tested: `rust/src/cli_env.rs` (`parse_bool_env`, `bool_env_value_parser`, `flag_enabled`, `flag_disabled`) wired into `rust/src/main.rs`'s `--silent` (the only clap bool arg with an `env` attribute in the crate) and into every ad-hoc boolean read — the full converted-site list is in `docs/case-studies/issue-1181/README.md`. `solver_helpers::env_bool`/`env_bool_with_extra_truthy` now delegate to the same table so there is one spelling vocabulary crate-wide. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1181_boolean_environment_parser.rs`. The one intentional exception: `FORMAL_AI_FULL_TRUST` (`rust/src/bounded_autonomy.rs`) keeps its exact-`"1"` sentinel because it is a security opt-in, not a UX switch. `rust/src/translation/pipeline.rs`'s `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG` read is deferred to the issue-#1174 change that owns that file. |
| R1181-7 | `FORMAL_AI_SILENT=1 formal-ai chat --prompt …` (and `=true`, `=yes`, `=on`, case-insensitive, and their false-y counterparts) no longer errors, and the non-clap `verbose_enabled()` read of the same variable honours the same spellings. | Delivered and tested: the `value_parser = formal_ai::cli_env::bool_env_value_parser` attribute on `--silent` (the `SetTrue` action is preserved, so a bare `--silent` flag still works), and `dialog_log::verbose_enabled()`'s second read goes through `!flag_enabled("FORMAL_AI_SILENT")`. Pinned by `silent_switch_now_accepts_one_as_the_issue_reported` and `bool_env_value_parser_maps_spellings_to_clap_results` in the same test file, which assert the exact truth table for the reported failing value. |

## Issue #1187 Optional GitHub Credentials in Every Workflow

Issue [#1187](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1187) (E151,
part of the E127 umbrella #1183): tokens are "not mandatory, but optional in
all cases". One resolver chooses a GitHub App, then one `AUTOMATION_TOKEN`
secret, then `github.token`; bot pull requests get their checks by dispatch
instead of waiting for approval; isolated tests use orphan branches in this
repository; cross-repository work degrades to a report. R1187-1 through
R1187-6 are the issue's R1–R6; R1187-7 and R1187-8 are its automated and
manual tests. Existing-file migrations are deferred edits recorded in
`docs/integration-manifest.md`; the history and the #1124 check evidence
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1187/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1187-1 | Every workflow that writes to GitHub takes its token from one resolver — GitHub App (`AUTOMATION_APP_ID` + `AUTOMATION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) → `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` → `github.token`; `FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN` is replaced; nothing skips or fails on a missing token; the layer is printed to the log and the job summary. | Implemented: `.github/actions/automation-token/action.yml` resolves the three layers, writes the layer to the log and `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and exposes `can-create-repositories` (true only at the App layer); `cross-org-duplication.yml`, `dependencies-latest.yml`, `e2e-isolation.yml` and now `self-authored-pull-request.yml` use it. The self-authored job no longer reads `secrets.FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN`: it passes the resolved token as `GH_TOKEN` and, for the composite action's unchanged contract, as `FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN` only when the layer is not `default`. `release.yml` reads no `FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN`. Pinned by `the_resolver_action_implements_the_three_layers`, `no_workflow_or_action_reads_a_github_token_secret_but_the_automation_names` and `the_self_authored_workflow_resolves_its_token_and_dispatches_checks` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs`. The action is a local mirror of link-foundation/.github `resolve-github-token` (link-foundation/.github#1), not a call to it. |
| R1187-2 | At layer `default`, the workflow that opened or pushed the pull request dispatches every `pull_request` workflow on the head commit; `layered-ci.yml`, `evidence-check.yml` and `workflows.yml` gain `workflow_dispatch` with `mode: checks`. | Implemented: `self-authored-pull-request.yml` calls `.github/actions/dispatch-checks` at layer `default` once the bot pull request exists, and the dispatcher runs `gh workflow run` on the head branch for every `pull_request` workflow that declares the checks mode. Every `pull_request` workflow now declares it (`mode` with `options: [checks]` and a `pull-request` input). Three are left out, each named with its reason in `every_pull_request_workflow_declares_the_checks_mode_or_a_reason_not_to`: `desktop-release.yml` (a dispatch publishes release assets), `external-benchmarks.yml` (a dispatch runs the credentialed full-slice jobs) and the authoring workflow itself. `release.yml` is dispatched too since its dispatch defaults to checks (R1187-3). The resolver now takes the `AUTOMATION_*` secrets as inputs from each caller. A composite action cannot read `secrets`, so it had failed to load (pinned by `the_resolver_takes_its_secrets_as_inputs_from_every_caller`). The dispatcher's own script, run against this repository's workflows with a recording `gh`, dispatches every other `pull_request` workflow in checks mode on the bot branch (`rust/tests/web/issue-1187-release-dispatch.test.mjs`); whether the dispatched runs satisfy a branch rule is part of the post-merge acceptance run (R1187-8). |
| R1187-3 | `release.yml` gets a checks-only dispatch mode that is the default, and every release, publish and tag job requires an explicit release mode and `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `release.yml`'s `workflow_dispatch` declares the checks-mode `mode` input (`options: [checks]`, so `actions/dispatch-checks` may dispatch it) and a `release_mode` that defaults to `checks` (`bump_type` defaults to `patch`); `manual-release`, `changelog-pr`, the Pages deploy and the release preflight's release mode each require an explicit `instant` or `changelog-pr` mode and `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, and `detect-changes` names its push and pull-request triggers instead of excluding dispatch. A checks dispatch runs only the lint and test jobs. Pinned by `release_dispatch_needs_an_explicit_mode_and_main` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs` and its JavaScript twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1187-release-dispatch.test.mjs`: both parse every job of `release.yml`, take each one with a `write` permission, and require that every `||` alternative of its condition that admits `workflow_dispatch` names an explicit release mode and the main ref (a writing job with no `if:`, the preflight, must guard its own dispatch alternative the same way), that `release_mode` defaults to `checks`, and that no deferred #1187 R3 row remains in `docs/integration-manifest.md`; the manifest tolerance the rule used to have is removed. |
| R1187-4 | Workloads needing a separate test tree use an orphan branch `e2e/<purpose>/<run_id>/<name>` built with `git checkout --orphan`, an `e2e-task` issue and a pull request based on that branch, all closed and deleted at the end; a separate repository only when the resolver reports `can-create-repositories: true`; this repository's `pull_request` workflows ignore `e2e/**` bases. | Implemented: `.github/workflows/e2e-isolation.yml` builds the orphan branch from only the named paths and opens the `e2e-task` issue and the pull request. Its cleanup closes both and deletes the branches. When the resolver reports `can-create-repositories: true`, the isolated tree is pushed instead to a new private repository `<owner>/formal-ai-e2e-<run_id>`. That repository carries the tracking issue and pull request, and the cleanup deletes it. Every `pull_request` workflow carries `branches-ignore: ['e2e/**']`. Pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs` by `orphan_branch_isolation_needs_no_credential` and `every_pull_request_workflow_is_dispatchable_and_ignores_e2e_bases`. |
| R1187-5 | Cross-repository work opens issues directly at layer `app`/`token` when it can write there; at layer `default` it writes findings to its report and keeps one tracking issue in this repository. | Implemented: at layer `default`, `.github/workflows/cross-org-duplication.yml` drops `--open` with a `::warning::` and uploads `data/meta/cross-org-duplication.lino` as the report. It keeps one tracking issue in this repository titled "cross-org duplication findings (default credential layer)". It edits that issue while it is open and opens a new one only when none exists (job permission `issues: write`). Pinned by `cross_repository_work_keeps_one_tracking_issue_at_the_default_layer`. At layers `app` and `token`, the scan opens issues in the owning repositories through `--open`. |
| R1187-6 | `CONTRIBUTING.md` gains a "GitHub credentials" section: the three layers, `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` as the only token name, the optional GitHub App, and that nothing needs configuring. | Implemented: the "GitHub credentials" section of `CONTRIBUTING.md`, pinned by `contributing_states_the_credential_rules` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs`. The section's claim that the unit test fails on any other token secret name now holds: `no_workflow_or_action_reads_a_github_token_secret_but_the_automation_names` rejects every `secrets.*` GitHub credential outside the `AUTOMATION_*` names. |
| R1187-7 | An automated test parses every workflow and composite action and fails on a GitHub-token secret other than the two `AUTOMATION_*` names, on a `pull_request` workflow without `workflow_dispatch`, and on a release job that can run on dispatch without an explicit mode and the `main` ref. | Implemented: `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs` (at that path, not under `ci_cd/` as the issue named it) parses every workflow and composite action and fails on a GitHub-token secret other than the `AUTOMATION_*` names (`no_workflow_or_action_reads_a_github_token_secret_but_the_automation_names`), on a `pull_request` workflow without `workflow_dispatch` or without the `e2e/**` ignore (`every_pull_request_workflow_is_dispatchable_and_ignores_e2e_bases`), and on a writing `release.yml` job that a dispatch can reach without an explicit mode and the `main` ref (`release_dispatch_needs_an_explicit_mode_and_main`, with no manifest exception since the R1187-3 guard was applied). The rule is checked per job and per `||` alternative, and its JavaScript twin `rust/tests/web/issue-1187-release-dispatch.test.mjs` also checks that it rejects a dispatch alternative missing either the mode or the ref. `every_pending_manifest_row_names_a_file_and_an_issue` keeps the remaining deferred rows honest. |
| R1187-8 | Manual acceptance: with no `AUTOMATION_*` configured, labelling an issue `formal-ai-solve` produces a bot pull request whose checks all start without approval, and the summary reads `layer default`. | Pending: the acceptance run itself has not happened, and it cannot happen from this branch. An `issues: labeled` event always runs the default branch's workflow file, so labelling an issue before the merge would exercise `main`'s pre-#1187 `self-authored-pull-request.yml`. The mechanism is tested now in `rust/tests/web/issue-1187-release-dispatch.test.mjs`. First, the resolver's own `resolve` script runs with every `AUTOMATION_*` input empty and writes `layer=default`, the fallback token and the summary line ``layer: `default` ``. Second, `self-authored-pull-request.yml` reacts to the `formal-ai-solve` label and calls `dispatch-checks` at layer `default` with the author's `pull-request` output. Third, the dispatcher's own `dispatch` script, run against this repository's workflows with a recording `gh`, dispatches every `pull_request` workflow except the three named exclusions with `--ref <bot branch> -f mode=checks`, `release.yml` included. What remains after the merge is one observation: label one issue `formal-ai-solve` on a repository with no `AUTOMATION_*` configured, then check that the bot pull request's checks start without an approval click and that the job summary reads `layer default`. |
